questions.q: Of the seven columns in orders_raw, which one did the crawler infer incorrectly, and as what type?
options: product_category — inferred as bigint instead of string
quantity — inferred as double instead of bigint
unit_price — inferred as string instead of double
order_date — inferred as string instead of date
questions.explain: order_date came back as a plain string even though it holds date values, because CSV carries no native type information.

questions.q: Why does the crawler's classifier default to string for a column like order_date rather than guessing date?
options: The crawler always infers every column as a string by default, regardless of its contents
It's a safe, conservative default — under-committing on type is better than guessing wrong and making values unreadable
Glue Crawlers are structurally incapable of inferring date types from any file format
CSV files are not allowed to contain date-formatted columns
questions.explain: The crawler samples values and makes a reasonable but conservative guess; CSV's lack of built-in typing makes date columns a common place for this to happen.

questions.q: What does `date_parse(order_date, '%Y-%m-%d')` do in an Athena query?
options: Casts the string column to a usable date value at query time, without changing the stored schema
Permanently rewrites the order_date column in the underlying S3 CSV files
Deletes rows where order_date cannot be parsed
Renames the order_date column in the Glue Catalog
questions.explain: date_parse is a query-time cast — it doesn't modify the Catalog schema or the underlying files, which is exactly why it fits this project's one-off use case.

questions.q: According to the lesson, when does editing the Glue Catalog's column type directly (instead of casting at query time) become the right call?
options: Only if the S3 files are stored in Parquet format instead of CSV
Once a table is load-bearing for multiple downstream jobs that repeatedly depend on it
Never — Athena always requires casting at query time regardless of use case
Only when the table has fewer than five columns
questions.explain: A query-time cast is fine for a one-off ad hoc query; a schema edit makes more sense once a table is relied on repeatedly, as the lesson notes will be true for the curated dataset in the Intermediate project.

questions.q: What is "schema drift" in the context of this lesson?
options: A decline in Athena query performance over time
The physical movement of data between AWS regions
The process of partitioning a table by date
A column's inferred type or structure changing between crawler runs as the underlying source files change shape
questions.explain: Schema drift describes how a crawler's inferred schema can shift if source files add, remove, or reformat columns between runs — worth checking after every crawler run.
